subject: TTFT & streaming transport: targets, WebSocket vs SSE, and next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@fastpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: TTFT targets + streaming transport

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on requirements and what we can demo next week:

Summary of requirements you shared:
- TTFT target: <= 120ms p95 for short responses (<= 32 tokens) under steady load.
- Longer responses: acceptable to see higher TTFT, but first-chunk must arrive within ~200ms.
- Concurrency: expected peak concurrency ~350 concurrent sessions, average 90.
- Throughput: ~2.1M tokens/day with 30% spiky traffic windows.
- Streaming: you prefer WebSocket for bi-directional UX but can consider SSE if it simplifies scaling; chunk cadence: ~150-300 token chunks (or every 150ms max).

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben to propose an initial configuration for a sandbox (model variant + quantization + batching) that hits the TTFT target under expected concurrency.
2) FastPay to share the short TTFT test set and any internal measured latencies (you mentioned a small test harness).
3) We run a focused sandbox test (48-72h) to produce a performance report and suggested fallback policies (SSE fallback, smaller chunk sizes).
4) Align on contract SLO wording and any procurement timelines.

Attachments: you mentioned a PDF of internal requirements — please send that (or drop in the Drive link) so we can incorporate precise payload sizes.

I'll kick off the sandbox proposal now; Ben, copying you for the config. Alex, is Wednesday or Thursday next week good for a short demo of the sandbox results?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the summary. A few clarifications and I attached our internal TTFT requirements PDF for the sandbox run.

Clarifications / notes:
- The 120ms p95 is for the gateway-to-client first byte (end-to-end), not just model execution. We will factor in network + client render.
- For the chunk cadence, our UX team is experimenting with 200-token packets; acceptable cadence is anything that yields an incremental UI update every ~200ms on average.
- We can provision a separate test environment for the sandbox (AWS account) and share a small harness that simulates our message mix.
- Procurement: we have an existing framework; if the sandbox looks good we can move to a 6-month pilot with an SLA appendix.

Attached: FastPay-TTFT-requirements.pdf (summary + sample payloads).

Wednesday 10am PT works for a short demo.

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: TTFT targets + streaming transport

Alex / Naomi — thanks for the details and the PDF, very helpful. I've sketched an initial sandbox and measurement plan below. High level goals: validate end-to-end TTFT <= 120ms p95 for short responses, and prove stable chunk cadence for streaming UX.

Initial sandbox config (proposal):
- Model: opt-6.7b-quant (verified low-latency variant) + KV-cache warm path enabled.
- Hardware: 2 x A10g or equivalent for model serving behind an edge proxy (we'll size exact instance types after the first run).
- Networking: colocate agents in the same AWS region as your test account to minimize network delta.
- Transport: primary: WebSocket streaming with incremental chunking; fallback: SSE if connection count / proxy overhead is lower in real tests.
- Chunking: start with 150-token max chunks and 150ms pacing; we'll sweep incrementally (150/200/300 tokens and 100/150/200ms pacing) to find the best UX/economics trade-off.
- Batching/concurrency: dynamic batching with a max aggregate batch window tuned to keep per-request latency < 30ms added by batching.

Measurement plan:
1) Baseline model-only TTFT (local) across per-request token sizes.
2) End-to-end TTFT with client harness (you provide) across 90 -> 350 concurrent sessions.
3) Observe p50/p95/p99, first-chunk arrival, and payload-chunk inter-arrival times.
4) Run a 48h spike window (2x traffic) to validate autoscaling + fallback triggers.

Deliverables:
- A perf report (p50/p95/p99, chunk cadence histogram, cost estimate).
- A short runbook for integration: transport choice, retry windows, and suggested SLO wording.
- redwood-slo-proposal.xlsx with suggested SLA lines for the pilot.

Questions / asks for FastPay:
- Can you share the harness repo or a container image and an initial concurrency profile?
- Any network middleboxes or WAFs that could terminate long-lived WebSocket connections?

I can spin up the initial sandbox config this week if you grant access to the test AWS account. Naomi — I recommend we share the Drive folder with FastPay after Alex confirms access.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
